title: Write the forecast first
hook: After seeing the result, how well can you remember your original forecast?

knows: basic arithmetic and reading a small table
doesNotKnow: Compare a recorded prior forecast with a retrospective recollection.

misconception: The quantities in this case can be combined without checking their reference, denominator, or information boundary.
objective: Compare a recorded prior forecast with a retrospective recollection.
keyState: Both complete computed cases are visible as retained observations; the question-case picture survives Reset.

claims.text: Before an event you record probability 0.2, and the event occurs. What squared-error score does that recorded forecast receive? Toy inputs A=[0.2, 1]; B=[0.8, 1].
claims.source: Local explicit hypothetical assumptions in spec.ts and model.ts; not participant measurements.

claims.text: Computed results: [[0.6400000000000001, 0.2, 1], [0.03999999999999998, 0.8, 1]]. Labels: Squared error, Forecast, Outcome.
claims.source: compute() in the lesson-local model.ts; finite numeric operations over the explicit inputs.

claims.text: A recorded forecast can be scored against the outcome without relying on later memory. The retrospective probability gives a different score, but rewriting the old forecast after seeing the event does not improve the original prediction.
claims.source: The two controlled cases in spec.ts; scope limited to these toy inputs and displayed model rule.

claims.text: A new toy case uses Forecast P=0.8, Outcome 0/1=1. What is Squared error? Answer: 0.04.
claims.source: compute() applied to the contrasting new input case; source list is an idea pointer only.

recall.question: A new toy case uses Forecast P=0.8, Outcome 0/1=1. What is Squared error?
recall.why: Applying the stated toy rule to the new inputs gives 0.04. The result depends on these assumptions; it is not a universal behavioral response.

sourceProvenance.text: After events, people believe they predicted them better than they did, the hindsight bias (Fischhoff, 1975; Fischhoff & Beyth, 1975).
sourceProvenance.caveat: Original list says figures are approximate and papers were not individually rechecked. No empirical source is verified by this build.

meaningfulDifference: Compare a recorded prior forecast with a retrospective recollection.
